visualReview.notes: Inspected seven current portable views. The skewed main hall, brown upper band, flat roof, recessed doorway and white portico with two round posts read clearly. The MÜZE lettering faces outward and the step plinth meets the original ground.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected seven current shared-material views including the dated north-up placement. Cream scored walls, brown panel band and the pale canopy remain distinct. The mapped hall ring and independent north canopy read separately in the placement overlay.

mediumFiReview.notes: Inspected all 23 current context, detail and transition frames. All four authored levels retain the main body and portico silhouette. The closer levels restore the scored wall courses, door mullions, coping and lettering.

geographicReview.notes: Original four-point hall outline from OpenStreetMap way 1411083878. The site way and two neighboring buildings were resolved separately. The 128 m original field was fixed before the floor and sections. The current unmasked field view shows both columns and the stepped entry meeting the site surface. Coarse datum and local threshold grades are approximate.

fidelityReview.scope: Akhisar Museum’s mapped single-storey exhibition building as photographed in February 2025, including its north entrance canopy and glazed doorway, cream scored walls, brown tiled upper band, flat parapet roof and low entrance steps. The separately mapped administration building, storehouse, outer gate and garden exhibits are excluded.
fidelityReview.notes: The dated exhibition hall uses the observed single-storey proportions, pale ruled plaster, brown upper panels, white canopy and sheltered glazed entry. Overall height, unseen roof treatment, secondary walls and the exact canopy depth are estimated. The independently mapped administration and storage buildings remain separate.

imageryReview.notes: Used three existing Qualla originals by Pragdon, matched to exact Commons SHA-1 bytes, pinned revisions and explicit CC0 self dedications. The photographs were used for the exterior only. Exhibit photographs and the floor plan display were not used.

validation.sharedCaptureScope: dated exhibition hall and north entrance on its independently mapped geographic placement

limitations: OpenStreetMap way 1411083878 supplies the four original corners of the main exhibition hall. Qualla’s three exact CC0 photographs from February 2025 establish the white north portico, cream wall courses, brown upper panels and recessed glazed entry.

Model height, canopy depth, door width, plain secondary elevations and the flat roof concealed by the brown parapet are original estimates. The camera EXIF locations support the north entry but have metre-scale position uncertainty. Coarse DEM contact and threshold geometry remain approximate.
Scope is the single-storey exhibition building. The administration building, storehouse, gate, trees, loose exhibits and interiors remain outside the asset.
The independent 128 m terrain field was preserved before choosing the floor and geometry. The original surface was sampled without flattening or height adjustment. No reference pixels are embedded.
